youtube.title: Why Is an Hour 60 Minutes? (Not 100)
youtube.description:
We count everything in tens, except time. In 1793 France tried a 10-hour day with 100-minute hours, and it lasted less than two years. So why does the strangest number still run your day?

From Sumerian scribes counting in sixties 4,000 years ago, to Egyptian sundials and stretching hours, Ptolemy's 'first small part' and 'second small part', and the minute hand that only appeared around 1690, this is how 60 minutes conquered the world.
